Total number of questions — 20

Development of Delhi-Srinagar
(Garhwal) road as a National
Highway
*101. SHRI RAJ NATH SINGH: Will
the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
has declared Delhi-Mawana-Kotdwara-
Pauri-Srinagar (Garhwal) road as a National
Highway;
(b) whether it is also a fact that
Government has completed the said road
upto Satpuli but it is still pending with the
present Government for completion of
width; and
(c) by when, the said road would be
completed and the reasons for the slow
progress of work?
Conservation of medicinal plants and
traditional knowledge
*102. SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) the elements of the National
Programme for Promoting Conservation of
Medicinal Plants and Traditional
Knowledge;
(b) the organizational structure set up
to implement various objectives of the
programme and in what manner the
finances are being delegated to the
participating States; and
(c) the number of States which have
identified the sites for the conservation of
medicinal plants, the details of the
medicinal plants, State-wise and
area-wise?

34
Shortcomings in TRAI
Act
*103. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRA-
SEKHAR: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Telecom Regulatory
Authority of India (TRAI) Act which came
into being in 1997 and in which many
amendments have already been made, still
has many shortcomings for which further
amendments are required;
(b) if so, whether the shortcomings have
been identified by Government;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) by when, necessary amendments are
proposed to be made in the said Act?
Grant of carbon credits to domestic
companies
*104. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government has set up any
national level mechanism to calculate and
grant carbon credits to domestic companies;
(b) whether Government has made any
estimates of the potential for domestic
industry in carbon trade;
(c) if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
and
(d) whether Government proposes to
hold capacity building programme for the
private and public industries in carbon
trade?
Universal Service Obligation
Fund
*105. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that two private
telecom operators have been found making
false claims and drawing excess subsidy
from the Universal Service Obligation
(USO) Fund for providing services in rural
areas;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the steps taken by Government
against them for making wrong subsidy
claims?
Indians deported from Arabian
countries
*106. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of OVERSEAS INDIAN
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether many Indian workers have
been deported to India from some Arabian
countries;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the action taken to ensure that Indian
workers are not harassed?
JNNURM funds for AP
*107. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY: W ill the Minister of
URBAN DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government had allocated
sufficient funds to the State Government
of Andhra Pradesh for the current year for
the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban
Renewal Mission (JNNURM);
(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) the projects undertaken for this
purpose during the last three years, State-
wise especially in Andhra Pradesh; and
(d) the amount allocated and spent under
this mission in each State during the current
year and the progress achieved so far?
Settlement of claims under PLIS
*108. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has fixed any
maximum time limit within which death
claims must be settled under the Postal Life
Insurance Scheme (PLIS);
(b) if so, the number of claims settled
within this time limit; and
(c) the average time taken for different
death claims settled under the Postal Life
Insurance Scheme (PLIS) during the last
three years?
Indian workers in Middle-East

SHRI PRASANTA

List of Questions for  WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Wednesday, the November 21, 2007/Kartika 30, 1929 (Saka)

(Ministries: Commerce and Industry; Defence; Home Affairs; Information
and Broadcasting; Labour and Employment; Parliamentary Affairs; Rural
Development; Textiles)
Total number of questions — 125
69
National Authority for geographical
indicators for intellectual property
rights
291. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a National
Authority to determine geographical
indicators is necessary to secure against
possible infringement of intellectual
property right of any community or region;
(b) if so, whether it is a fact that the
country does not have such national
authority to determine geographical
indicators;
(c) if so, the reasons for delay in setting
up such national authority and what steps
are being taken to expedite the process;
and
(d) whether Government has made
transitory arrangement in this regard?
Non-availability of residues detection
facilities
292. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that imported
agricultural commodities were not subjected
for the presence of pesticides residues due
to non-availability of residues detection
facilities; and
(b) how many consignments of our
agricultural commodities have been returned
by other countries on account of presence
of unacceptable levels of pesticides residues
in the past five years and details of
commodities and countries?
Report on SEZs by MPs panel
293. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether a panel of Member of
Parliament has reportedly submitted the
Report titled "The functioning of Special
Economic Zones" on June 20, 2007;
(b) whether the panel has opined that
existing rules under SEZ Act had failed to

70
protect the farmers' interests and 'New
Special Economic Zones' should be put on
hold;
(c) if so, what are the other
recommendations made by the panel; and
(d) whether Government propose to
bring forward draft legislation to amend the
Act during the ensuing Winter Session of
Parliament?
Abnormal increase in cement price
294. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether there has been an abnormal
increase in cement price especially in some
States;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the action taken to regulate the price
of cement?
High heavy metal content in herbs
exported
295. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Indian herbal
exports often face rejection on grounds of
high heavy metal content and the presence
of other unwanted ingredients; and
(b) if so, the details of action taken by
Government to prevent such rejection due
to high heavy metal content?
Trade with Gulf, Western Asian and
African countries
†296. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL: W ill the Minister of
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be
pleased to state:
(a) the extent of trade carried out by the
country with the Gulf, West Asian and
African countries;
(b) whether Government propose to
hold talks with Gulf Co-operation Council
on Free Trade Agreement and with West
Asian and African countries on Investment
Promotion Agreements; and
(c) if so, the details of the benefits
derived as a result of these agreements?
Setting up of Leather Industry Parks
†297. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have proposed
setting up of five leather industry parks in
the country;
(b) if so, the name of the cities where
these Leather Industry Parks will be set
up;
(c) what schemes have been formulated
by Government for providing employment
to maximum people in these parks; and
(d) what is the maximum number of
persons likely to get employment in these
parks and what steps have been taken by
Government for simplification of export
of leather products?
Plethora of regulations for foreign
entrepreneurs
298. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the World Bank's recent report mentioning
about existence of plethora of Government
regulations that foreign entrepreneurs have
to cope with while doing business in India;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

(b) if so, when the reforms being
undertaken in this regard will fructify as
we are even much behind the pace of such
reforms done in China; and
(c) will time-bound reforms be done so
that in foreseeable future, the tedious red-
tape no longer adversely affects our
business scenario?
EOUs in the country
